The coffee is familiar. The neighborhood is new.

Lantern Coffee, the small roaster that has run a single café in the North Loop since 2019, says it will open a second shop on Central Avenue in Northeast Minneapolis next spring. The company announced the lease this week. (Demo story; the roaster is fictional.)

A second location is a bigger step than it sounds. Think of it like a band playing its first show in a new city: the songs are the same, but nobody in the room owes you anything yet. Lantern will need to hire and train a new crew, keep its roasting schedule steady for two counters, and earn regulars who have never heard of it.

The company says the new space will roast nothing on site; beans will still come from the North Loop roaster. That keeps costs down, and it also means the original shop becomes a small supply hub. If either location has a bad month, the other one feels it.

Lantern has not said what the build-out will cost or how many people it plans to hire. Those details are worth watching, because they tell you whether this is a careful test or the start of a bigger push.

For now, it's a local favorite betting that good coffee travels about two miles.
